Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Ιωάννης και οι μαθητές αυτού», with the rank word left off; the page's own head line for him reads «Οσιος Ιωαννης».

Read out of the Охридски пролог's entry headed „Преподобни оци грузијски.“ for 7. мај ст. ст., whose body says „Началник свих ових христољубивих мисионара био је свети Јован Зедазнијски.“ Свети is no rank and Преподобни in the heading is the `venerable` this folder already carries in `types`; **Зедазнијски is kept**, because it is a by-name from Mount Zaden and not a rank word `honorific.js` composes — and keeping it is what holds this folder out of the gate's eight-folder `? "јован"` fold, which the bare form would have made nine. The name stands in the body's naming sentence and not in the heading, which names nobody at all.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 7 mai — «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Zedazneli, dimpreună cu 12 ucenici din Georgia»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ιωάννης και οι μαθητές αυτού»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day the Romanian calendar keeps the company, and it is plainly the same company: John out of Syria and the twelve chosen to go into Iberia, whose names the page prints as «Σίω, Δαβίδ, Αντώνιος, Θαδδαίος, Στέφανος, Ισήδωρος, Μιχαήλ, Πύρρος, Ζήνων, Ισέ, Ιωσήφ και Άβιβος». **Thirteen head lines, thirteen names, so thirteen folders**, and the corpus already holds every one of them, so the whole company is upgrades and no folder is created. **`shio-of-mgvime` is the one exception and is not touched**: its `greek` row is already `venerated`, on 4 Φεβρουαρίου, so a reader may not move it; that he is listed here too is a second Greek day and is left in the report. **The Greek adds the whole story of the mission and no years at all**: the flight deeper into the desert when the crowds broke his stillness, the Theotokos appearing in a dream and commanding him to choose twelve and go to Iberia, the names written on separate papers and laid on the holy table, the night of prayer, the twelve papers an angel took from the altar into his hands before them all, the monk Euthymius left as abbot of the skete, the angel warning Bishop Eulogius of the Georgian capital of their coming, the bishop going out with clergy and people to meet them, the wonder like Pentecost by which John spoke Georgian, and their preaching through all Georgia and their veneration of the blessed places Saint Nina had passed, whom the page sends to 14 Ιανουαρίου. **No year, no hymn**, and the page does not say where any of the twelve settled afterwards — the sees and monasteries in their corpus names come from the Romanian side and nothing here is added to them. **His own head line is «Οσιος Ιωαννης»**, and the page's account of him is the fullest of the thirteen: the Syrian birth, the studies at Antioch, the self-reproach that called him a worm and not a man, the dispassion and the gift of wonders, the flight into the desert, the dream, the lots, and his death after he had counselled and blessed his disciples and communicated. **It gives him no year**, and the folder's existing birth interval is not touched.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 20.05.2026 (7. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни оци грузијски.“

attestations.note: **The heading names nobody and the body enumerates the whole company, so the citation above is the heading whole** — „Преподобни оци грузијски.“ — per BRIEF-SERBIAN.md §4's synaxis ruling and the coordinator's first ruling for an enumerated company, and the Serbian name form is read out of the body's naming clause: „А имена су њихова: Авид, Антоније, Давид, Зинон, Тадеј, Иса, Издериос, Јосиф, Михаил, Пир, Стефан и Шијо.“ — twelve bare forenames, no rank word on any of them and no epithet, with Началник свих ових ... био је свети Јован Зедазнијски standing before the list for their leader. **The identification is the set and not the name**: the corpus already keeps these thirteen men together on this very menologion day, out of doxologia's «Sfântul Cuvios Ioan Zedazneli, dimpreună cu 12 ucenici din Georgia» and saint.gr's «Όσιος Ιωάννης και οι μαθητές αυτού», and the Prologue's twelve names map one-to-one onto the twelve folders, eleven of them unmistakably — Антоније, Давид, Зинон, Тадеј, Јосиф, Михаил, Пир, Стефан, Шијо, Иса for Ise of Tsilkani and Издериос for Isidore of Samtavisi — which forces the twelfth, Авид for Abibus of Nekresi, because it is the only slot and the only name left. **`types` was deliberately not touched on any of the thirteen.** Преподобни in that heading heads a company of thirteen whose own folders carry ranks three other calendars gave them — `hieromartyr` and `bishop` for Abibus, `hierarch` and `bishop` for Jesse, `stylite` for Anthony — and a rank word covering a whole company is not evidence about one man's own grade; adding it could make `honorific.js` compose a different word to every reader, which is the `boris-michael-of-bulgaria` ruling. **No `locations` were taken**: Georgia is a country. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. **This folder is the company's leader and the heading's „Преподобни“ is the `venerable` it already holds**, so nothing was added to `types` here either. „Началник свих ових христољубивих мисионара био је свети Јован Зедазнијски.“ gives him the by-name Зедазнијски, **which is kept** — it is the mountain of Zaden his own life is named from, not a rank, and `honorific.js` does not compose it. **Keeping it is what holds this folder out of the gate's `? "јован"` set of eight and the `? "ιωαννησ"` set of ninety-odd**, which was measured and not assumed: the bare «Јован» would have made a ninth. **NO DATE WAS TOUCHED**: this folder already holds a birth of „late 5th century“ from doxologia, and the entry's „У VI веку“ dates the mission rather than the man and would not sharpen it. New to the corpus from this page and on no other account of him: that the mission came **two hundred years after Saint Nina preached the Gospel in Georgia**; that the twelve were **solemnly received by the prince of the land and by its catholicos**, whom this book names Евлалије where saint.gr's angel announces them to a bishop Eulogius and doxologia names neither — **the catholicos is named here and kept out of the life on purpose**, because `eulalius-the-hierarch`'s display name is the bare Eulalius and `related-floor.test.mjs` would ask for a row in both directions for a man who is not this one; that the people **gathered about them in crowds**; and that they **founded many monasteries and left many disciples after them**.
